title: Etienne Bourdeaux to Maarten van der Goes, Berlin, 31 January 1801 (DECODE R1944)

documents.shelfmark: Nationaal Archief, 2.01.08, Ministerie van Buitenlandse Zaken 1796-1810, inv. 257, fol. 294; DECODE R1944

plaintext.source: Ministry clear copy of no. 16, fol. 295, imaged as DECODE R1946 image 3 (IMG_R1946_I13417_P3.png).

transcription.source: Authenticated DECODE scans of R1944 and R1946 (clear copy, Sept 2026); Nationaal Archief public scans NL-HaNA_2.01.08_257_0432 and _0433 (code groups, 14 Nov 2026).
transcription.notes: The clear copy was transcribed in Sept 2026. The code groups were transcribed on 14 Nov 2026 from the Nationaal Archief scans, with their superposed marks: 115 groups measured (the earlier figure of about 110 was an estimate by eye); a single AI transcription, not checked by a person, 5 groups marked doubtful. Corrections: 'vertrek' -> 'renvoy', 'positiver' -> 'positiever' on second reading.

system.summary: A numerical Dutch diplomatic nomenclator of one- to three-digit groups with superposed marks, attributed by DECODE to S. E. Croiset.

diacritics.note: Bars, ticks, waves, dots and crosses over the figures.

system.notes: Key not identified; groups not aligned to the clear copy.

prior_solution.where: The ministry's clear copy, fol. 295, misfiled under DECODE R1946.

conditions.human_role: Supplied authenticated DECODE access and posed the target.

solution.what: Retrieved the two R1944 scans: cipher groups only, with closing and signature.
Viewed the neighbouring records R1945 and R1946; R1946 image 3 is a clear sheet headed N. 16, Berlyn 31 January 1801, (get.) Bourdeaux.
Re-read the scan (corrected renvoy, positiever); checked consecutive folio stamps 294/295 and that ~90 words fit ~110 code groups.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): the contemporary clear copy and its translation, copied from NOTES.md to texts/; the ~110 code groups were never transcribed (project work)

Looked for a transcription of the code groups: none in the folder, none on DECODE R1944 (the public record page lists two images only, and DECODE full-size images need a login). Found the Nationaal Archief's own public scans of inv. 257 (601 scans); the letter is scans 432 (fol. 294r) and 433 (fol. 294v), the clear copy scan 434.

Transcribed the code groups line by line from the full-size Nationaal Archief scans, with the mark over each group (texts/R1944_transcription.txt): 115 groups in 11 lines, 5 marked doubtful. No key, so no decoding check; the pair 237: 927+ recurs where the clear copy has 'zyn Cyffer' twice, and 927+ again near the end where it has 'nieuw Cyffer'. By Claude (session of 14 Nov 2026), not checked by a person.

outcome.method_basis: The ministry's contemporary clear copy of the despatch (fol. 295, N. 16, Berlin 31 Jan 1801) was found misfiled as image 3 of DECODE R1946 and transcribed; the code groups were not decoded.
outcome.notes: Plaintext from the contemporary clear copy; the code was not decoded group by group.

texts.label: R1944, Etienne Bourdeaux, Berlin, 31 Jan 1801 (clear copy, no. 16)
texts.summary: The Dutch chargé d'affaires in Berlin reports that Rosenkrantz does not know why he was dismissed and supposes his cipher was taken and copied by a servant; Lusi says more definitely that the desk holding his cipher was forced open, which is why Schuer was to be sent to Petersburg with a new cipher. So the letter, itself in cipher, reports a compromised codebook.
